questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses offered and the academic staff. Also learning other approaches and academic traditions. And traveling: meeting people, getting new experiences and living in a different place.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My stay was great, really did not want to back home at the end of it. And absolutely loved Uni of Edinburgh academically.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not that easy. There was a bit of red tape and a lack of information regarding registering and getting settled. That was on the part of the recipient uni, however. The Erasmus part of the process was seamless.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received great assistance on several occations. Often information was lacking, but talking to one of the contact persons resolved it each time. I think personal assistance in adminstrative matters is more common in Scotland than in Denmark (that is, less automated), so that was a bit of a cultural lesson. My student advisor and others were extremely helpful and accommodating.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was really good. Also the students at my dorm were good at making us feel welcomed (I stayed at Riego Street in Edinburgh).

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I registered quite late but still got something right away.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Edinburgh, it is the only option. Also the housing market is crazy, so you can't do much better by letting something private (unless you know people).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was too expensive. Exchange students have no network so they are easy to exploit--it is sad that it happens. It is basically funneling money from Erasmus to the for-profit uni (uni-administered student housing used to be much cheaper at Uni of Edinburgh).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a bit of confusion regarding where to register arrival but other than that it was hassle-free.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Do not remember entirely but think it was going to a certain meeting at a certain time and get a "yes you are here" stamp.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was the student advisor who was generally available for all sorts of questions. It was really nice to have such a general point of contact.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Again, it did not work when I did it online--but then I went to the office where they did it and I was immediately registered at courses that I had wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: When in doubt, ask someone. Do not hesitate to reach out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My three lecturers were absolutely great. Really passionate and knowledgeable.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did elective courses on level 10--which are third year courses--and there were both undergrads, grad students and PhD students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Fewer people in class, more time for questions, more time with professors (I only took electives so it is really not comparable to regular classes).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender and environment
Race and ethnicity
Sociology of medicine

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sociology of medicine was a revolutionary course to me, big recommendation. Very medically technical and so politically relevant as an approach to scientific aspects of modern politics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was as expensive as in Denmark; housing was much more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many cool societies!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All of them. So much happening, especially uni-related.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on your interests. Go visit several societies to find out which seem nice.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking! You cannot go in winter, so try and take a week or two during the summer break to go to the Cairngorms or the Trossachs or around Inverness.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. However, Scots (and Brits in general) are not comfortable with (even partial) nudity which is a common sight in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language (haha). Also Indian food. And pub culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is not that different from Denmark culturally or academically.
Do not despair if it is hard to meet locals; as a friend you are an ephemeral investment.
People are younger than at Danish unis.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many places to study and so many campuses; check as many out as possible.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The classes. Also the people that I made friends with.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Writing my final essays.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
